ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the circuit diagram, the inverting input terminal “−” of the ideal operational amplifier is connected to a node; the left side of this node is connected to V1 through a 10 kΩ resistor, and above it, feedback comes back from the output terminal Vout through a 100 kΩ resistor. The non-inverting input terminal “+” of the operational amplifier is connected to another node; the left side of this node is connected to V2 through a 10 kΩ resistor, and downward it is connected to ground through a 100 kΩ resistor. The output terminal is labeled Vout on the right side. Reasoning: The non-inverting terminal voltage is obtained from V2 through voltage division by 10 kΩ and 100 kΩ, V+ = [100 kΩ / (10 kΩ + 100 kΩ)] V2 = (10/11)V2. For an ideal op-amp and with negative feedback present, V− = V+ = (10/11)V2. Write KCL at the inverting input node: (V− − V1)/10 kΩ + (V− − Vout)/100 kΩ = 0. Multiplying both sides by 100 kΩ gives 10(V− − V1) + (V− − Vout) = 0, namely Vout = 11V− − 10V1. Substituting V− = (10/11)V2 gives Vout = 11·(10/11)V2 − 10V1 = 10(V2 − V1). Given V1 = 10 mV, V2 = 50 mV, so Vout = 10(50 − 10) mV = 400 mV.

method.method_draft: First describe the image topology and identify the two source paths. By superposition, set V2 = 0: the non-inverting input is grounded, so the V1 path is an inverting amplifier with gain −100k/10k = −10, giving contribution Vout1 = −10V1. Next set V1 = 0: the non-inverting input voltage is the divider value V+ = 100k/(10k+100k)·V2 = (10/11)V2, and the closed-loop gain from V+ to output with Rin = 10 kΩ to ground and Rf = 100 kΩ is 1+100k/10k = 11, giving Vout2 = 11·(10/11)V2 = 10V2.
